sentences.text:
Smt. P. Kamalamma, Medak District And 3 ... vs T. Gopal, Medak
District And Ano on 21 June, 2023

Author: G.Radha Rani
Bench: G.Radha Rani
 The Honourable Dr.Justice G.Radha Rani
 M.A.C.M.A.No.1371 Of 2011
Judgment:

This appeal is filed by the appellants - claimants seeking enhancement of compensation from Rs.2,75,000/- to Rs.6,00,000/- aggrieved by the award dated 01.04.2011 passed in M.V.O.P.No.71 of 2010 by the Special Judge for Trial of Offences under SC & ST (POA) Act-cum-V Additional District & Sessions Judge, Medak at Sangareddy.

entities.text: SC & ST (POA) Act-cum-V Additional District & Sessions Judge, Medak at Sangareddy
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. The wife and children of the deceased filed the claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.6,00,000/- for the death of the deceased by name Pichakuntla Narsimulu in a motor vehicle accident on 05.01.2010 at 11:30 PM near Jana Priya Hotel near New Bus Stand, Sangareddy submitting that while he was proceeding on foot towards old Bus Stand from Jana Priya Hotel, a TATA Indica Car bearing No.AP 12 U 5737 came in a rash and negligent manner and hit the deceased from his behind, due to which he sustained severe bleeding injuries and while undergoing treatment in the Government Hospital, Sangareddy, succumbed to injuries.
The claimants contended that the deceased was aged 42 years and was earning Rs.6,000/- per month by doing labour work by the date of the accident.

Due to the sudden death of the deceased, the claimants lost the bread earner of the family and Dr.GRR,J macma_1371_2011 prayed compensation from the respondents 1 and 2, the owner and insurer of the TATA Indica Car bearing No.AP 12 U 5737.
3.
The respondents 1 and 2 filed separate counters denying their liability.

4. Before the Tribunal, the claimant No.1, the wife of the deceased was examined as PW.1 and got examined an eye-witness to the accident as PW.2 and got marked Exs.A1 to A6, the certified copies of the police records.

The respondent No.2 got examined the Motor Vehicle Inspector as RW.1 and got marked Exs.B1 and B2, the extract of the Driving License of the driver of the TATA Indica Car and the copy of the Insurance Policy.

5. The Tribunal on considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, awarded an amount of Rs.2,75,000 with costs and interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit and held the respondents 1 and 2 jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation amount.

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the award and decree dated 01.04.2011 by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (for short "MACT"), the claimants preferred this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation from Rs.2,75,000/- to Rs.6,00,000/- , as claimed by them.

7. They contended that the Tribunal committed an error in taking the age of the deceased as between 50-55 years instead of 42 years and applied multiplier 11 instead of 14 and erroneously considered the earnings of the deceased as Dr.GRR,J macma_1371_2011 Rs.3,000/- per month and deducted 1/3rd towards the personal expenses, though ought to have deducted 1/4th towards the personal expenses as per the judgment of the Sarla Verma & Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation 1 , as the dependants were 4 in number.

entities.text: GRR,J macma_1371_2011 Rs.3,000/- per month and
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

entities.text: Sarla Verma & Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal committed an error in not awarding any amount towards love and affection and prayed to enhance the compensation.
8. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants - claimants and the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 - Insurance Company.
9. On a perusal of the record, the Tribunal considered the age of the deceased as between 50-55 years, considering the evidence of PW.1, wherein she stated that he was 50 years old.
PW.1 was an illiterate woman.
She filed her evidence affidavit stating the age of the deceased as 42 years.
She also filed Ex.A4, the certified copy of inquest report wherein the age of the deceased was recorded as 45 years by the Investigating Officer.
The certified copies of the FIR along with the complaint marked as Ex.A1 and the charge-sheet marked as Ex.A2 would disclose the age of the deceased as 45 years.
The PME report marked as Ex.A6 also would disclose the age of the deceased as 45 years.
As all the police records were disclosing the age of the deceased as 45 years, the same can be accepted.

The Tribunal considered the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.3,000/- per month,
considering the deceased as a labourer and presuming that he might be earning Rs.100/- per day.

However, considering the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in C.Ramachandrappa v. The Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited2, wherein for the date of accident in the year 2004, the earnings of a coolie or a labourer is considered as Rs.4,500/- per month,
considering that the wage of the labourer was between Rs.100/- to Rs.150/- per day during the relevant point of time and the date of the accident in the present case is on 05.01.2010, the income of the deceased can be taken as at least Rs.4,500/- per month.

entities.text: C.Ramachandrappa v. The Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
11. As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited v.
Pranay Sethi & Others 3 , future prospects shall be considered even in the case of persons who were self-employed.

entities.text:
National Insurance Company Limited v.
Pranay Sethi & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the age of the deceased as 45 years, an addition of 25% is to be added.

Hence, the income of the deceased can be considered as Rs.4,500+ (25% of Rs.4500) = Rs.5, 625/-.
12.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma Case (cited supra), multiplier 14 is to be added for the person considered to be aged 45 years and 1/4thto be deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased 2011 ACJ 2436 2017 ACJ 2700 Dr.GRR,J macma_1371_2011 when the defendant family members were between 4 to 6.

In the present case also, the defendant Smt. P. Kamalamma, Medak District And 3 ... vs T. Gopal, Medak District And Ano on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153103132/
2 family members were 4 in number, the wife and 3 children of the deceased.

entities.text: P. Kamalamma, Medak District And 3 ... vs T. Gopal, Medak District And Ano
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the Tribunal erred in deducting 1/3rd towards the personal expenses of the deceased instead of 1/4th.
After deducting 1/4th towards the personal expenses, the monthly contribution of the deceased towards his family can be assessed as Rs.5,625/- (-) (1/4thof Rs.5,625/-) = Rs.4,219/-.

Accordingly, the loss of dependency can be calculated as Rs.4,219/- x 12 x 14 = Rs.7,08,792/-.
13.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi Case (cited supra), a conventional amount of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium and Rs.15,000/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses, to be enhanced at 10% in every three (03) years is to be awarded.

14. As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Company Limited v. Nanu Ram and Others4, the children of the deceased are entitled for parental consortium due to pre-mature death of their father for loss of parental aid, protection, affection, society, discipline,
guidance and training.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited v. Nanu Ram and Others4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, an amount of Rs.44,000/- each is entitled to the appellants - claimants towards loss of consortium.
An amount of Rs.16,500/- each is entitled towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Hence, the compensation that can be awarded to the claimants under various heads is as follows:
 S. No. Heads Compensation  Awarded  1. Loss of Dependency Rs.7,08,792/-
 2. Loss of Consortium Rs.1,76,000/-

3 . Loss of Estate Rs.16,500/-
 4. Funeral Expenses Rs.16,500/-
 Total: Rs.9,17,792/-
16.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Nagappa v. Gurudayal Singh & Others5 which was also subsequently followed in Ramla and Others v. National Insurance Co. Limited and Others6, held that:
"...there is no restriction that compensation could be awarded only up to the amount claimed by the claimants.

entities.text: Ramla and Others v. National Insurance Co. Limited and Others6
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In an appropriate case, where from the evidence brought on record if the Tribunal / Court considers that the claimants are entitled to get more compensation than claimed, the Tribunal may pass such award."

17. In the result, the M.A.C.M.A. is allowed enhancing the compensation from Rs.2,75,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal to Rs.9,17,792/- which is considered as just and reasonable with costs &
interest @ 7.5 % per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.2 - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the above amount within two (02) months from the date of this judgment.

On such deposit, the claimants are 2003 (2) SCC 274 2019 ACJ 559 Dr.GRR,J macma_1371_2011 permitted to withdraw the entire amount as per their shares fixed by the Tribunal on payment of deficit court fee on the enhanced amount.
